content.comment_body: Hello, Before starting, I want to clarify that I mainly use the [product_name] demo version for developing a test bench. I have created a program, and these four issues are the last ones I need to resolve: 1) I can't use a comma to perform calculations with mathematical operators, but I need to display values like 49.9833 or 49.983 in my program. 2) I need to block the value shown by one sensor on the screen when a second sensor is activated. 3) I want to activate a heating resistor to reach a specific temperature; programming the heating part is done, but connecting the resistor is problematic. 4) After reaching a target temperature, I need to increase the speed again, but only this step is giving me trouble. Thank you if you can help.

Firstly, it's difficult to assist if the documentation or diagram is not in English, and poor-quality screenshots with grids are hard to read. It’s better to upload your diagram as a ZIP file. Regarding your first question: [product_name] is limited to using 16-bit integers and does not support floating-point numbers. However, you can simulate decimals by scaling values in your calculations (for example, use multiplication and division to represent decimal points).
Thank you for answering my first question, and sorry for not thinking to switch the names to English. I'll try to save my file as a ZIP and make the names clearer.
Sorry to bother you, but do you know what file type I should use? I tried the [product_name] file and compressed it, but it didn't work. I used WinRAR for compression.
I've succeeded uploading, no more help needed for the file. Could you now help me with my other questions? Thank you.
I also use WinRAR. You need to select "ZIP" as the archive format, not "RAR".

analysis.insight_summary: The user is working on a test bench project using [product_name] demo and faces several functional limitations such as the inability to perform floating-point calculations, challenges in displaying sensor values conditionally, issues with controlling a heating resistor, and difficulties in changing speed after reaching a certain temperature. The software's restriction to 16-bit integer arithmetic creates confusion for users needing decimal operations. Users also struggle with exchanging project files due to file format incompatibilities.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the programming environment to easily handle decimal numbers, allow straightforward logical control of sensors and actuators, and support seamless file sharing in widely accepted formats. They are looking for capabilities to perform advanced calculations and dynamic control within the program.
